questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
The initial allocation of goods between three consumers is shown. consumer 1 consumer 2 consumer 3 total
Which assumption in relation to an indifference theory diagram is not correct?

options.B: The consumer may change their satisfaction-maximising objective.
options.C: The consumers may change their tastes and preferences.
options.D: The relative prices of products may change.

questions.questionText: Which type of efficiency is shown by the shift from long-run average cost curve 1 (LRAC ) to long-run average cost curve 2 (LRAC )? price LRAC LRAC O quantity

options.C: Pareto

questions.questionText: A firm wishes to maximise its revenue. Which condition must be met to achieve this goal?

options.C: marginal cost = marginal revenue

questions.questionText: The costs and revenue of four firms operating in a monopolistically competitive market are shown. total total total firm variable cost fixed cost revenue $m $m $m W 20 10 15 X 40 50 80 Y 300 300 500 Z 600 100 550 Which firms will continue to operate in the short run but will shut down in the long run?

options.A: X and W B X and Y C W and Z D Y and Z

questions.questionText: A firm at its current level of production finds that its short-run marginal cost is less than its short-run average variable cost. Which conclusion about the firm can be drawn from this information?

options.C: Average variable cost is greater than its average total cost.

questions.questionText: Steel producer X takes over its main competitor, steel producer Y. What would X expect to happen to the price elasticity of demand for its product and its long-run average cost as a result of this takeover? price elasticity long-run of demand average cost

options.C: increase decrease

questions.questionText: What is an example of an external cost?

options.C: labour costs

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand for and supply of a good and the marginal social costs (MSC) for that good. MSC costs, revenue S y x z w D O Q output Assuming there are no external benefits, which area measures the net social benefit at output OQ?

options.A: x B x – y C x + y D x – y – z

questions.questionText: What would definitely result from the divorce of ownership and control?

options.C: greater productive efficiency

questions.questionText: One reason for market failure is the existence of public goods. Which policy option is appropriate for addressing such a market failure?

options.A: direct provision of the good by the government
options.B: provision of detailed information to consumers
options.C: subsidising firms that currently produce the good
options.D: the adoption of maximum price controls

questions.questionText: In 2020, the governor of California issued an order to ban the sale of new vehicles from 2035 that are powered by petrol or diesel fuel. Which type of government policy is this?

options.C: nationalisation

questions.questionText: The diagram illustrates a monopsony labour market in which the government has imposed a minimum wage. MCL W wage rate S = ACL W W minimum wage W
Economics textbooks state that labour is a derived demand for a firm in imperfect competition. How is the demand curve for labour derived?

options.A: by multiplying the average physical product by the average revenue
options.B: by multiplying the average physical product by the marginal revenue
options.C: by multiplying the marginal physical product by the marginal cost
options.D: by multiplying the marginal physical product by the marginal revenue

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the Lorenz curves for Norway (N) and India (I). cumulative percentage line of of income perfect equality N I 0 100 cumulative percentage of households What can be concluded from a comparison of the Lorenz curves?

options.A: India is more likely to have lower indirect taxes and a public sector education system than Norway.
options.B: India is more likely to have a progressive income tax system and means tested benefits than Norway.
options.C: Norway is more likely to have a progressive tax system and public sector pensions than India.
options.D: Norway is likely to have a higher percentage of tax generated from indirect taxes and privately funded pensions than India.

questions.questionText: A reason for government intervention in the workings of the economy is to attempt to correct a market failure. Sometimes, though, government failure may occur. What is not a possible reason for government failure?

options.A: Governments may have to make decisions on the basis of out-of-date information.
options.B: Governments may make decisions that reduce negative externalities.
options.C: The extent of the market failure may be difficult to judge.
options.D: When circumstances change, a government may be unable to respond quickly.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to support growth in the economy’s fishing industry. Which policy is likely to achieve sustainable growth in the fishing industry?

options.A: giving more modern fishing boats with larger nets to workers who fish for a living
options.B: paying bonus payments for larger fish catches to workers who fish for a living
options.C: setting up a fish cooperative so that workers who fish for a living receive a higher price for the fish that they catch
options.D: subsidising the building of a fish farm in order to encourage workers who fish for a living to switch from sea fishing

questions.questionText: Four citizens have each been unemployed for the past six months. Which citizen would not be characterised as being structurally unemployed?

options.A: worked as a coal miner but coal-fired power stations are now being closed and is not willing to retrain
options.B: no longer works in a town centre coffee shop because fewer people are buying goods in the town centre since a pandemic
options.C: cannot move with the firm that has relocated because of changing demand for its products
options.D: has many skills and is waiting to decide which job might be the most suitable

questions.questionText: In the diagram, OP is the equilibrium level of income and OQ is the full employment level of income in a closed economy. expenditure V U C + I + G T C + I R C 45° O P Q income What is the deflationary gap?

options.A: PQ B RV C TV D UV

questions.questionText: What is the most effective policy a government could introduce to reduce frictional unemployment?

options.C: reduce tax rates

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government sector, when will an increase in investment spending generate the largest increase in equilibrium national income?

options.A: when households have a high level of autonomous consumption
options.B: when households have a high level of compulsory saving
options.C: when households have a high marginal propensity to consume
options.D: when households have a high marginal propensity to save

questions.questionText: Which combination of policies is most likely to increase output? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: decrease budget deficit decrease interest rates
options.B: decrease budget deficit increase interest rates
options.C: increase budget deficit decrease interest rates
options.D: increase budget deficit increase interest rates

questions.questionText: A country is a net importer of oil. World oil prices have risen over the year. Assuming that all other factors remain the same, how is this likely to affect inflation, trade balance and unemployment in this country? inflation trade balance unemployment

options.C: increase worsen increase

questions.questionText: What would reduce the effectiveness of a supply-side stimulus to the economy?

options.A: an imposition of maximum hours in a working week
options.B: an increase in public sector spending
options.C: the provision of new training schemes
options.D: the relaxation of import controls on raw materials

questions.questionText: A multinational company (MNC) shifts its manufacturing capacity to a developing country. What is likely to be the short-run effect of this in the developing country? short-run balance employment investment of payments increases increases current account improves

options.C: yes no yes

questions.questionText: To indicate the changing income distribution, the Kuznets curve plots gross domestic product per capita against an economic variable X. What is variable X?

options.C: the price level

questions.questionText: Economists define the unemployed as being those who are not in work but are actively seeking work. Other groups of people in the population of working age include those classed as inactive or self-employed. Which groups of people are included as part of a country’s labour force? unemployed inactive self-employed

options.C: yes yes no

questions.questionText: The table shows some United Nations population statistics for 2010 and estimates for 2050. total total urban urban population population type of region population population population population urbanised urbanised (m) 2010 (m) 2050 (m) 2010 (m) 2050 (%) 2010 (%) 2050 more developed 1237 1275 930 1100 75 86 less developed 5671 7875 2556 5186 45 66 least developed 855 1673 249 914 29 55 Which relationship can be confirmed from the table?

options.A: The least developed regions have the largest urban populations, actual or predicted, in both years.
options.B: The more developed regions have the lowest growth rate of urbanisation between 2010 and 2050.
options.C: The type of region with the greatest total population in 2010 is predicted to have the greatest rate of population growth by 2050.
options.D: The type of region with the greatest urban population in 2010 is predicted to have the highest level of urbanisation by 2050.
